vulnerabilities.title: 'PHP2Shell' Critical PHP Flaws (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) - NCSC Patch-or-Isolate Alert Forces UK Councils, NHS Boards and Met Police Sites Offline
affected_products: PHP (unpatched supported branches; check php.net advisory for exact versions)
vulnerabilities.summary: UK government and public sector. Press reports (STV News, Insurance Business, Lancashire Evening Post) say the NCSC, with EU and Australian counterparts, urged immediate patching of two critical PHP flaws nicknamed 'PHP2Shell' (CVE-2026-109618/109619, both reported at CVSS 9.2) that can allow unauthenticated remote takeover of a web server. NCSC advice: patch at once; if not possible apply PHP's temporary mitigations; if that is also not quick, consider taking affected systems offline. In response, at least seven of Scotland's 32 councils and six NHS health boards pulled public websites, and Edinburgh and Oxford councils, South Ribble Borough Council, the Met Police and Golden Jubilee Hospital were reported affected. Most sites were restored within hours to the next morning after patching. No confirmed in-the-wild exploitation was found in the sources; the takedowns were precautionary. NHS England Digital also lists PHP advisories dated 20-21 Oct. Details are from secondary reporting; NCSC primary text and PHP advisory were not retrieved. UPDATE 23 Oct: multiple security vendors now report in-the-wild exploitation - watchTowr (honeypot sightings), Patchstack (multiple confirmed incidents), Aikido and Cloudflare (early attack attempts); the Dutch NCSC says it is receiving partner signals of active weaponisation, while CISA had not observed exploitation as of its 21 Oct alert and the CVEs were not seen in KEV. Datadog states the widely circulated config workaround does not protect; only patching fixes it. No UK-specific compromise confirmed. UPDATE 24 Oct: fixed releases reported as PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 (PHP 8.1 and older unsupported; use vendor backports). Wiz, Tanium, Bitsight and Canada's Cyber Centre (AL26-026) have published guidance; KEV listing still not confirmed. UPDATE 25 Oct: SecurityWeek reports Mirai botnet operators joining PHP2Shell attacks and ASLR-bypass exploits emerging; Amazon threat intelligence reports first attempts from 17 Oct, ahead of the fix; joint NSA/CISA guidance urges immediate patching or taking unpatchable systems offline. Vendor accounts conflict on exploit reliability. KEV listing not confirmed. UPDATE 26 Oct: no new UK-specific compromise reported; NCSC guidance unchanged (patch to fixed releases or take unpatchable systems offline). KEV listing not confirmed. UPDATE 27 Oct: CISA added CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 to the KEV catalog on 26 Oct (alert 'CISA Adds Two Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog'), formally confirming in-the-wild exploitation (earlier 23 Oct CISA text said none observed). KEV due date not retrieved. VulnCheck reports an ASLR-aware x86-64 exploit against CVE-2026-109618 (customers only). No new UK-specific compromise confirmed; NCSC guidance unchanged. UPDATE 28 Oct: no new UK-specific compromise reported; NCSC CTO weekly summary (w/e 25 Oct) still urges immediate PHP mitigation. UPDATE 29 Oct: search summaries cite a Lords statement (Baroness Lloyd) that 32 central government services were unavailable and four partly affected, mostly precautionary, with no confirmed compromise of central government or wider public sector systems; some early compromise claims withdrawn. Amazon and honeypot reports of wider exploitation (incl. 35 live shells) remain unconfirmed by UK officials. UPDATE 30 Oct: no new UK-specific compromise reported; press (Irish News) cites a minister saying there was no breach of Budget security after the PHP flaw; NCSC guidance unchanged. UPDATE 2 Nov: no new UK-specific compromise reported; NCSC guidance unchanged (patch to fixed releases or isolate). UPDATE 4 Nov: UK press reports 32 UK government services went offline as a precaution and a minister told the Lords it did not mean anyone was hacked; patch uptake reported low. No new UK compromise confirmed.
recommended_actions: Upgrade to PHP 8.5.12 / 8.4.27 / 8.3.36 / 8.2.35 or a vendor-backported fix; replace unsupported 8.1 and older.
Inventory all PHP-based web servers (CMS, intranets, legacy portals, third-party hosted council/NHS sites) and patch to the fixed PHP releases from php.net immediately.
Do not rely on the circulated config-only workaround (reported ineffective); prioritise patching.
Where patching is delayed, apply PHP's published temporary mitigations and restrict exposure via WAF/reverse proxy; isolate if neither is possible.
Hunt for webshells and unexpected child processes from PHP handlers; review web logs for anomalous requests since 2026-10-20.
Confirm suppliers and hosting providers have patched before restoring sites.

kql.name: Web server PHP process spawning shell
kql.description: Possible PHP2Shell post-exploitation: PHP/Apache/nginx parents spawning shells or download tools. Untested; tune.
kql.query:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("php","php-fpm","php-cgi","php-fpm8","apache2","httpd","nginx","w3wp.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","curl","wget","nc")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine

kql.name: New PHP files written in web roots
kql.description: Hunts newly created .php files in common web directories (possible webshells).
kql.query:
DeviceFileEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActionType == "FileCreated"
| where FileName endswith ".php"
| where FolderPath has_any ("/var/www","/usr/share/nginx","\\inetpub\\wwwroot","htdocs")
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine

iocs.context: Press coverage of PHP2Shell listed no IPs/domains/hashes; hunt on behaviour.

vulnerabilities.title: Commercial Refrigeration Controller Attacks Hit European Supermarkets - NCSC Confirms Small Number of UK Food Businesses Exploited
vulnerabilities.vendor: Unconfirmed (commercial refrigeration controller vendors; not named in sources retrieved)
vulnerabilities.summary: UK corporate (food supply chain). Search-result summaries report coordinated attacks on 2 Nov against internet-facing commercial refrigeration controllers across Europe (Germany, Romania and the UK reported supermarket-related incidents; EU urged action on 4 Nov). The NCSC said it knew of a small number of UK instances where vulnerable technology was exploited, mainly small meat-processing/food businesses, and its chief executive described UK impact as minimal. No group claimed responsibility. Exploited vendor, CVEs and techniques were not confirmed; earlier research (Frostbyte10 on Copeland, Claroty on Danfoss/Copeland XWEB) and a UK Cyber Defence finding of 800+ exposed UK retailer fridge controllers show the exposure is long-standing. Primary sources (NCSC, Al Jazeera) could not be retrieved; treat details as unverified.
recommended_actions: Remove refrigeration/OT controller management interfaces from the internet; place behind VPN/allow-listing.
Apply vendor firmware updates for Copeland/Danfoss controllers and change default credentials.
Enable independent temperature alarms and manual monitoring for cold-chain assets.
Report incidents to the NCSC.

kql.query:
let controllers = dynamic(["10.0.0.0/8"]);

| where DeviceAction !in ("deny","drop")

| where ipv4_is_in_any_range(DestinationIP, controllers)
| where DestinationPort in (80,443,502,8080,8443)

vulnerabilities.title: NCSC 'State of the Cyber Nation' Report: AI-Enabled Ransomware on UK Critical Infrastructure 'Highly Likely' by 2028; Government Web Services Being Checked After AI-Found PHP Flaws
vulnerabilities.summary: UK government. On 3 Nov 2026 the NCSC (CEO Richard Horne) published its State of the Cyber Nation assessment, judging it 'highly likely' that AI-powered malware will feature in ransomware attacks on UK critical national infrastructure by 2028. NCSC expects AI to accelerate existing tactics rather than create new attack routes, with attacker adoption uneven, and attributes exposure partly to underinvestment in cyber security. Reporting says government is checking its online services following AI-discovered PHP flaws (see PHP2Shell entry) and that organisations unable to patch should consider taking systems offline. Same day the government cut Cyber Essentials prices for micro/small/mid-sized firms (GBP 80-125 + VAT); the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill remains pending. This is a strategic assessment, not an incident; no new confirmed compromise of UK government systems was found in the 24h window. Details are from search summaries (NCSC page fetch blocked) and unverified.
recommended_actions: Prioritise patching internet-facing PHP estates to fixed releases or isolate them
Review ransomware resilience and offline backups for CNI-supporting services
Brief leadership on NCSC AI-threat assessment; align with Cyber Security and Resilience Bill readiness

vulnerabilities.title: WordPress Core Unauthenticated RCE (CVE-2026-87902) Exploited Within Hours of Disclosure - Dutch NCSC Advisory 4 Nov; Exposure Relevant to UK Public Sector Websites
affected_products: WordPress Core 4.7.0-7.1.1 (under specific theme/server conditions); fixed in 7.1.2, 7.0.6, 6.9.9, 6.8.10
vulnerabilities.summary: Search-result summaries report a critical WordPress Core flaw (CVE-2026-87902) enabling unauthenticated remote code execution under specific theme and server conditions, with attackers reportedly exploiting it within hours of disclosure (eSecurityPlanet). The Dutch NCSC published an advisory dated 4 Nov 2026. No UK-specific compromise or UK NCSC alert was found in the window. Relevance: many UK councils, NHS bodies and charities run WordPress, and this follows the PHP2Shell web-server patching scramble. Dates and details are unverified secondary reporting; the publication date of the exploitation report could not be confirmed and may predate the window. A separate earlier chain ('wp2shell', July 2026) affected 6.8-7.0 and was patched in 6.9.5/7.0.2/6.8.6.
recommended_actions: Update WordPress Core to 7.1.2, 7.0.6, 6.9.9 or 6.8.10 and confirm auto-updates are working.
Review web roots for unexpected PHP files, new administrator accounts and unknown plugins/themes.
Apply WAF rules from your vendor; inventory WordPress sites across the estate including third-party hosted ones.

vulnerabilities.title: 3AM Ransomware Affiliate Encrypts UK School Estate - Bitdefender Suspects AI-Assisted Intrusion; Bristol City Council Schools Data Leak Claimed by Wallstreet
affected_products: Windows endpoints/servers in UK school estate (unnamed)
vulnerabilities.summary: UK public sector (education/local authority). Bitdefender reporting (BleepingComputer, eSecurityPlanet, 3-4 Nov) says a 3AM ransomware affiliate encrypted about 37 of nearly 50 machines in an unnamed UK school estate between 10 and 19 Sept 2026; Bitdefender suspects parts of the intrusion were AI-assisted but evidence does not prove an AI model drove the attack. Separately, ITPro (4 Nov) reports at least 320,000 files tied to 39 schools published on a dark-web site after an attack on an education platform, and the Wallstreet group's 27 Oct claim naming Bristol City Council remains unattributed/unverified by the council. No new confirmed compromise of central UK government systems in the window. Details are from search-result summaries only and are unverified.
recommended_actions: Review school/education estate segmentation, offline backups and EDR coverage
Hunt for 3AM-style tooling: shadow copy deletion, mass encryption, RMM/remote access abuse
Monitor leak sites for council/school data and warn affected parents/staff of phishing risk
Align with NCSC ransomware guidance and report incidents to NCSC/ICO

kql.name: Shadow copy deletion / recovery inhibition
kql.description: Untested hunting query for ransomware precursors.
kql.query:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (FileName =~ "vssadmin.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("delete shadows","resize shadowstorage")) or (FileName =~ "wbadmin.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "delete") or (FileName =~ "bcdedit.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("recoveryenabled no","ignoreallfailures"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine

kql.name: Mass file rename burst on servers
kql.query:
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d) and ActionType == "FileRenamed"
| summarize Renames=count() by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, bin(Timestamp,5m)
| where Renames > 500

vulnerabilities.title: Legal Aid Agency (MoJ) Breach Scope Widened - Records Back to 1978 and HMPPS Probation Data Found in Stolen Set
vulnerabilities.vendor: UK Ministry of Justice / Legal Aid Agency
affected_products: Legal Aid Agency online services (2025 intrusion)
vulnerabilities.summary: UK central government. Per an agency update dated 2026-10-14 reported by CyberSecurityNews and GBHackers, forensic review of the 2025 Legal Aid Agency (Ministry of Justice) breach found the exfiltrated data goes further back than first disclosed: about 250,000 records pre-date 2007 and the earliest verified record is from 1978. Investigators also found probation data from HM Prison and Probation Service (HMPPS) in the stolen material. The agency states it has no indication the data has been published or shared. This is a scope update to an older incident rather than a new intrusion, but it materially raises the sensitivity (applicants, defendants, probation subjects) and is the most significant UK government item found in the window. Details come from secondary reporting; the primary agency/MoJ notice could not be fetched.
recommended_actions: Organisations that supply or share data with MoJ/LAA should check for notifications and prepare for phishing and fraud aimed at affected individuals.
Monitor leak sites and dark-web markets for LAA/HMPPS-related data.
Review third-party and legacy-data retention: purge or archive-isolate pre-2007 records where legally possible.
Brief helpdesks on social-engineering using legal-aid or probation context.

kql.description: Hunts inbound mail using breach-themed lures. Tune keywords.

| where SenderFromDomain !endswith "justice.gov.uk" and SenderFromDomain !endswith "gov.uk"
| project Timestamp, SenderFromAddress, RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, UrlCount, AttachmentCount

iocs.value: No technical indicators published for this scope update.
Data exfiltration of legacy case records; follow-on fraud/phishing against affected individuals

vulnerabilities.title: HMICFRS Warns Hackers Have Repeatedly Compromised Suppliers Holding UK Police Data - Most Contracts Lack Ongoing Cyber Assurance
affected_products: Third-party suppliers to UK police forces
vulnerabilities.summary: UK police and public sector. A gblock article dated 28 Oct, citing The Record (27 Oct), reports that HMICFRS found hackers have repeatedly compromised third-party suppliers holding British police data since 2021, and that most supplier contracts carried no ongoing cybersecurity assurance. Context: earlier supplier breaches exposed officer data (e.g. ID-card supplier incidents affecting Met and Greater Manchester Police). Primary HMICFRS/Record text was not retrieved; details are secondary and unverified. Supply-chain exposure for forces and other public bodies using similar suppliers.
recommended_actions: Inventory suppliers holding police/public-sector personnel data and require ongoing security assurance in contracts
Review supplier access and data-sharing; monitor for phishing targeting officers/staff
Check NCSC supply chain security guidance

vulnerabilities.title: Carry-over: 'FortiBleed' - Stolen Fortinet Firewall Credentials Include UK Government, Embassy, Council and NHS Accounts Offered for Sale
affected_products: Fortinet FortiGate appliances (reported ~70,000-86,000 devices / credential sets, 194 countries)
vulnerabilities.summary: No new development found in the 2026-10-15 window (carry-over). Telegraph-led reporting from July 2026 says Russian-speaking actors harvested credentials from tens of thousands of Fortinet firewalls ('FortiBleed'); leaked/for-sale lists reportedly include IT staff at UK embassies (Thailand, Mauritius), local-authority staff (Derbyshire, Waltham Forest), and NHS, energy and medicine-supplier logins, with access priced up to ~$60,000. Counts vary by source (SOCRadar: 86,644 credentials). No formal state attribution and no NCSC/Fortinet PSIRT/CISA confirmation was found. This is NOT new in the 24h window - no fresh development was found - and is carried only because it is the most UK-government-specific credential exposure identified. Confidence is low; treat as a lead for credential rotation and exposure review.
recommended_actions: Rotate all credentials and secrets on FortiGate devices and any accounts authenticating through them; invalidate VPN sessions.
Patch FortiOS to the latest release and review for unknown admin accounts, config changes and exposed management interfaces.
Check dark-web/credential-leak monitoring for your domains.

kql.name: Fortinet - new admin accounts or config changes
kql.description: Detects admin/user creation and configuration changes in FortiGate CEF logs.
kql.query:
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DeviceVendor == "Fortinet"
| where Activity has_any ("Add admin","Add user","Edit admin","Configuration changed","Attribute configured") or AdditionalExtensions has "cfgpath"
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, SourceIP, SourceUserName, Activity, Message
| sort by TimeGenerated desc

iocs.context: Per press reporting; no formal attribution.

vulnerabilities.title: Citrix NetScaler ADC/Gateway Zero-Days Under Active Exploitation - NCSC and NHS England Alerts; UK Follow-on SAML Flaw Pending (CVE-2026-88771, CVE-2026-88772, CVE-2026-107406)
affected_products: Hybrid Secure Private Access deployments using NetScaler
vulnerabilities.summary: UPDATE 2026-10-15: No NCSC update newer than the September advisory was found in the window; the NCSC continues to urge prompt mitigation, says it is still assessing UK impact, and warned that exploitation attempts would rise once patches and technical details were public (which has now happened: public PoC and mass 'spray and pray' scanning reported 2026-10-14). Mandiant says exploitation began in early September and affected North America and Europe. Sophos warns patching alone does not evict an attacker already on an appliance. Prior detail: UPDATE 2026-10-14: Help Net Security reports NetScaler exploitation has escalated from stealthy zero-day targeting into widespread 'spray and pray' attacks, fuelled by a published root-cause analysis and a public proof-of-concept exploit; Citrix and CISA confirm active exploitation and note patching alone may not remove access from an already-compromised appliance. No UK-specific victims were identified in search. The UK NCSC has told UK organisations to mitigate Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway flaws promptly after confirming reports of active exploitation of CVE-2026-88771 (unauthenticated command execution, CVSS 9.5, affects default configurations) and CVE-2026-88772 (memory overflow leading to code execution or DoS, CVSS 9.5, requires DTLS, which is on by default for VPN virtual servers). Citrix disclosed them on 2026-09-27 (bulletin CTX697096) and CISA added both to KEV the same day with a 2026-09-30 federal deadline, but researchers report webshell deployment since early September, i.e. exploitation preceded disclosure. NHS England's National CSOC issued alert CC-4858 (2026-09-28) rating further exploitation 'almost certain', and a follow-on alert CC-4865 (updated 2026-10-09) covers a separate critical SAML memory-overflow flaw, CVE-2026-107406, which NHS CSOC assesses as likely to be exploited but which is not reported exploited. NetScaler is common in UK central government, NHS trusts, councils and corporate remote-access estates; no UK-specific exposure count was found (global counts range from ~21,000 to ~50,000 exposed instances depending on scanner). Post-exploitation reporting describes web shells (WHIPSHOT), a Python tunneller (SLAPSHOT) and a custom remote-management implant (Platypus) with a replaced customsnmpd. Patching alone does not evict an implant: appliances exposed since early September should be treated as potentially compromised. NOTE: this item is a carry-over/escalation from late September rather than a first report inside the 24h window; it is included because it is the only confirmed, actively exploited issue with direct NCSC and NHS England UK advisories and a pending follow-on CVE. Indicator detail comes from secondary vendor blogs - verify against Citrix's IoC scanner and the NCSC page. Primary pages could not be fetched directly in this run.
recommended_actions: Treat public PoC availability as raising urgency: patch internet-facing NetScaler now, and rebuild/replace any appliance exposed since early September rather than only patching.
Upgrade to 14.1-73.37 / 13.1-64.23 or later and then apply the fix for CVE-2026-107406 as it lands; do not rely on mitigation alone.
Run Citrix's IoC checker and review appliances for the listed file paths, unexpected .deb files and replaced customsnmpd; treat hits as full compromise.
Rotate credentials and secrets stored on or reachable from the appliance, and invalidate VPN sessions.
Restrict management and gateway exposure; forward NetScaler logs to Sentinel.
Follow NCSC and NHS England Digital cyber alerts CC-4858/CC-4865 for updates.

kql.name: Citrix NetScaler - exploitation artefact file paths
kql.description: Applies if NetScaler/Linux telemetry or file-integrity logs reach MDE. Otherwise port to FIM or syslog.
kql.query:
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(45d)
| where FolderPath has_any ("/vpn/scripts/linux/","/var/netscaler/logon/LogonPoint/custom/")
| where FileName in~ ("nsgclient18.deb","nsg64.deb",".ctxs.receiver") or FileName endswith ".deb"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| sort by Timestamp desc

kql.name: Citrix NetScaler - post-patch outbound connections from appliances

vulnerabilities.title: CISA KEV Adds Cisco ASA/FTD SSL VPN DoS (CVE-2026-76418) and GitLab CVSS 10 RCE (CVE-2026-97229) - Edge/DevOps Exposure Relevant to UK Public Sector
affected_products: Cisco Secure Firewall ASA and FTD (SSL VPN)
vulnerabilities.summary: Not UK-specific: no UK victim identified. Secondary reports (The Hacker News, Rescana) say CISA added two exploited flaws to KEV on 29 Oct: a Cisco ASA/FTD SSL VPN denial-of-service (CVE-2026-76418) with no vendor IoCs published, and a GitLab unauthenticated RCE (CVE-2026-97229, CVSS 10.0) via a crafted regex in CI/CD config, linked to a failed exploitation attempt disclosed by Alpine Linux. Federal due date 1 Nov. Both product families are common in UK government and corporate estates (VPN perimeter, source-code/CI platforms), so exposure is plausible. Dates conflict slightly between outlets and primary CISA/vendor pages were not retrieved. Context: UK window otherwise surfaced no new dated UK government incident; the NCSC PHP2Shell alert (rank 1) remains the main UK-relevant item. UPDATE 2 Nov: reporting indicates CISA KEV listing on 29 Oct with a federal remediation deadline of 1 Nov (now passed); Cisco has not published campaign-specific IoCs and no actor attribution is public. Sources differ on DoS vs wider compromise impact; rely on Cisco advisory cisco-sa-asaftd-tunnel-dos-s6mgkb75.
recommended_actions: Patch GitLab and Cisco ASA/FTD to fixed releases per vendor advisories
Inventory internet-exposed GitLab instances and ASA/FTD SSL VPN endpoints
Review GitLab CI/CD configs and runner logs for anomalous regex-heavy or newly added pipeline definitions
